title: An advocate who labels the first act as accidental makes every subsequent act read as confusion rather than coordination
body:
- Casting the first act as accidental removes intent from the sequence, so the standards that gate the use of force no longer attach.
- With intent removed, every subsequent act is read as justified confusion rather than as part of a coordinated use of force.
- The incident is thereby relocated from a category of sanctionable misconduct to one eliciting sympathy as a tragic mishap.
conversion: A coordinated use of force is reframed as a cascade of justified confusion, neutralizing the standards built to evaluate intentional harm.
